Mid Evaluation · FYP-2

What the project is for

Reconstruct a surgical scene in 3D from one laparoscope camera — then anticipate how the tissue deforms next.

Reconstruct4D geometry from monocular video Complete · FYP-1

Predict ahead1–3 frames, with confidence Implemented · Module 6

Research question

Can future tissue geometry be predicted from ordinary surgical video — and can the system say how much to trust each prediction?

Progress 2 / 3
Mid Evaluation · FYP-2

Metrics chosen, and what they measured

Accuracy — not yet ahead

  • Constant velocity beats us at every horizon, on all ten videos.

Direction — clearly learned

  • Cosine +0.57 at t+1. A model that learned nothing reads 0.00.

Uncertainty — calibrated

  • Spread across five futures tracks realised error, r = 0.69.

Progress 3 / 3 · the base papers
Mid Evaluation · FYP-2

What we build on, and where we go past it

The work we build onWhere it stops → what we add
EndoGaussian · Deform3DGSsurgical reconstruction
Only ever describe what already happenedWe match them from one camera, then predict forward.
PointRNNpoint-cloud forecasting · our main learned baseline
Rigid outdoor scenes, one answer, no confidenceDeforming soft tissue — and ours says how much to trust it.
Luo & Hu, CVPR 2021the first point-cloud diffusion model
Generates shapes; does not forecastOurs is that idea made conditional on time.
TPG-VAE · SurgVistasurgical anticipation
Flat pixels, and told the instrument’s actionWe predict 3D geometry, and we are not told the action.
No published method does all of it at once — predict the future, in 3D, on soft tissue, from a single camera, and say how confident it is.

The key finding
Mid Evaluation · FYP-2

The model knows which way tissue moves — not how far

t+1+0.57
t+2+0.40
t+3+0.26
t+5−0.01
t+10−0.49
A model that learned nothing would read 0.00 everywhere. The direction is right; the distance is wrong — which is a far more tractable problem, and both fixes are implemented.
GASR · S26-017-R-GASR
10
Our strongest result
Mid Evaluation · FYP-2

The model knows when it should not be trusted

r = 0.69spread vs realised error
5futures sampled per input
5×uncertainty growth over 10 frames

When the five sampled futures disagree, the prediction really is worse — so the system can flag its own weak moments. A model that is confidently wrong is unusable in theatre; one that says “do not trust me here” is usable even when imperfect.

Stated carefully: this is correlation between predicted spread and realised error. Some of it may reflect that busy moments are both harder and more variable.
